description: Fleet health for every Beyou container: resources (cAdvisor), scrape targets (Prometheus up), host (node-exporter), the app DB from the DB's own side (postgres-exporter) and log/error volume (Loki). Backend JVM internals live in the consolidated service-health dashboard, linked below.

panels.description: Compose services currently reporting to cAdvisor (a stopped container drops out of this count, which is how you notice one died silently).
panels.title: Containers tracked

panels.description: One row per running Beyou container, merged from instant queries. CPU = cores used (5m rate); Memory = working set; Net = eth0 bytes/s; Uptime resets to zero on every restart.
panels.title: Containers

panels.description: CPU cores used per service (5m rate of cAdvisor's cumulative counter). A value of 2.0 = two cores busy. Flat 0 = idle, not dead.
panels.title: CPU (cores) by service

panels.description: Working-set memory per service: the bytes the kernel considers actively used by the container. This is the number to compare against the limit, not cAdvisor's raw usage (which includes page cache).
panels.title: Memory working set

panels.description: Working set divided by the container's declared memory limit. Services without a compose limit (no deploy.resources) show no line, which is honest: there is no ceiling to measure against.
panels.title: Memory % of limit

panels.description: Bytes/s in and out of the container's primary interface. A steady baseline is normal (SSE, polling); a ramp with no traffic change is usually a client retrying.
panels.title: Network (eth0) RX / TX

panels.description: Container writable-layer usage against its declared filesystem limit. Steady growth here is uploads/logs living in the container layer instead of a volume.
panels.title: Disk used %

panels.description: Seconds since the container started. Every sawtooth back to zero is a restart, so a crash-looping service reads as a comb.
panels.title: Uptime (resets = restart)

panels.description: up{job=...} for every job in prometheus.yml. 1 = the target answered its last scrape; 0 = down or unreachable. watchtower is absent in dev by design. This is scrape-level availability; deep health per service lives in GlitchTip's Uptime page.
panels.title: Scrape targets (1 = answering)

panels.description: Host CPU busy share (idle subtracted). A sustained 100% here with low container CPU in the Resources row = something on the host outside Docker (backup, scan, another stack).
panels.title: CPU usage

panels.description: Run-queue length 1/5/15m. Above the CPU count (node_cpu_seconds_total does not tell you that; the dashboard's system_cpu_count in the service-health board does) = threads waiting for CPU.
panels.title: Load average

panels.description: Host memory in use = total minus MemAvailable (the kernel's own available estimate, which accounts for reclaimable cache).
panels.title: Memory used

panels.description: Host root filesystem usage. This is the disk that holds docker volumes, so it is the one that fills when logs or the Loki store grow.
panels.title: Root disk used

panels.description: Host physical interfaces RX/TX. Contrast with per-container Network above: the difference is traffic between containers, which never leaves the host.
panels.title: Network (host)

panels.description: Seconds since the host booted. A drop means the whole box restarted, which explains every container restarting at once.
panels.title: Host uptime
Postgres (app DB, from the DB's own side)

panels.description: pg_up: 1 = the exporter holds a live connection to the database. The dashboard's DB liveness signal, independent of the backend's pool.
panels.title: Postgres up

panels.description: Backend processes (pg_stat_activity rows) summed over all databases, including the exporter's own. Compare with the backend's HikariCP panels: pool exhaustion shows here as a plateau at max_connections.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Total on-disk size of every database, summed.
panels.title: DB size

panels.description: Backend processes per database. A second, flatter line is the exporter itself; a spike here with low HTTP traffic is a connection leak or a long-running query.
panels.title: Connections by database

panels.description: Shared-buffer hits / (hits + reads) over 5m. Above 0.99 is healthy for an app DB; sustained dips below 0.95 mean the working set outgrew shared_buffers or cold-cache churn.
panels.title: Cache hit ratio

panels.description: Transaction commit and rollback rates. A rollback rate climbing toward commits means application code is erroring mid-transaction.
panels.title: Commits vs rollbacks

panels.description: Deadlock counter rate per database. Any non-zero sustained rate is a bug in lock ordering, not noise.
panels.title: Deadlocks

panels.description: Active locks by database (all modes). A persistent wall at one database means that DB is the contention point; the lock mode labels in Explore tell you which kind.
panels.title: Locks held

panels.description: Number of Beyou services that emitted at least one line detected as error in the last 5 minutes. 0 is the resting state; when it climbs, the panel below says which service.
panels.title: Services with errors (5m)

panels.description: Lines per 5m window per service, from Loki's index (volume_enabled). This is where a log flood becomes visible as a wall before anything alerts.
panels.title: Log volume by service

panels.description: Rate of lines Loki detected as error level, per service. Click a service in the legend, then Explore, to read the actual lines.
panels.title: Error lines by service
